status: content architecture draft; not wired into live UI
purpose: Cross-lesson knowledge map built from the Lesson 1-14 teacher-PPT curriculum. Course pages answer 'what is in this lesson?'; Explore system pages should answer 'how does this Korean system work across lessons?'.

systems.title: Numbers, counters, dates, time & money

lessonProgression.focus: Native vs Sino-Korean systems, counters, prices, dates
time: Native Korean hours + Sino-Korean minutes

exploreSections: counter form changes 하나→한, 둘→두, 셋→세, 넷→네, 스물→스무

systems.title: Tense, aspect, intention & conjecture

lessonProgression.focus: present polite conjugation -아요/어요; concept of stem + ending

practiceIdeas: choose the ending by speaker intention

systems.title: Speech levels, politeness & honorifics

lessonProgression.focus: polite self-introduction, 씨, avoiding direct second-person pronouns in the taught context
honorific nouns, verbs, particles, and counters
choice between less-formal -ㄹ래요 and more listener-centered -ㄹ까요?

exploreSections: speech level vs honorific: separate dimensions
practiceIdeas: convert one message across speech levels
choose a form based on relationship

systems.title: Connecting clauses, contrast & reasons

lessonProgression.focus: N(이)라서 and three-way comparison: -아/어서 vs (이)라서 vs 때문에

keyContrasts: A/V-아/어서 vs N(이)라서 vs N 때문에
practiceIdeas: explain why one connector sounds more natural in context

lessonProgression.focus: adjective -(으)ㄴ + N and irregular adjective forms
present verb -는 + N; relative-clause word order; 이/가 inside modifier
past/completed verb -(으)ㄴ + N; result-state reading with clothing verbs
안 + A/V and 못 + action verb
밖에 + negative predicate and quantity expectation
V-지 못하다; V-지 마세요; V-지 말고

systems.title: Irregular conjugation families

lessonProgression.focus: ㅂ and ㄹ inside adjective noun modifiers

exploreSections: trigger-based view: what following sound/ending causes the change?

systems.title: Word building & productive patterns

lessonProgression.focus: native/Sino-Korean/loanword vocabulary layers; school and country Hanja families
N + 하다 verbs such as 공부하다/숙제하다
expanded N + 하다 vocabulary such as 쇼핑하다/운동하다/전화하다
adjective roots, color words, and ㅎ-irregular forms in noun modifiers
benefactive V-아/어 주다 and compounds such as 빌려주다
A-게 productive adverb formation; transport/service Hanja compounds

exploreSections: vocabulary layers: native Korean vs Sino-Korean vs loanword vs mixed
where short and long negation go with N+하다 predicates
stem + ending morphology across tense/aspect/irregular families
Hanja-derived suffix families such as -적/-성/-화/-자/-원/-인/-생/-장/-점/-관 (enrichment, not teacher-PPT core)
practiceIdeas: spot mixed words such as 선생님 and 몸조리

lessonProgression.focus: Place + 에 + 있다/없다 and position words
static/destination 에 vs activity-location 에서; -(으)러 가다/오다
place goal 에 vs source 에서

systems.title: Particles & sentence roles

lessonProgression.focus: location 에 and subject marking with 있다/없다
에/에서 for place goal/source; 한테/한테서/께 for person goal/source

practiceIdeas: choose 은/는 vs 이/가 in taught contexts

lessonProgression.focus: asking where people/things are and relationship-sensitive forms
making plans and responding to negative questions
asking/giving directions in formal and informal styles
birthday, age, giving/receiving, and honorific family interaction
professor-facing formal speech and indirect refusal
social invitations, preferences, proposals, and text-message style examples
telephone routines, requests, health, gratitude, and promises
taxi/airport exchanges, service expressions, inviting/declining, prohibition/advice

designRule: Explore should progressively disclose these systems and link every system explanation back to the lesson(s) where the learner encountered it. It should not load every lesson pack on initial page load.
